- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or trending down, adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- In high-event periods (≥10 events/30d), model often underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer to forecast mean to account for supply shock or policy volatility.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model is trending up, reverse direction by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment reversal” lag error.
- In low-event periods (≤5 events/30d), model tends to overestimate mean reversion; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to avoid premature correction.
- If recent auction supply is CAP3 EU/PL/DE, and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model often underestimates price drop; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast mean.
- In multi-day auction windows (e.g., 3+ consecutive CAP3 EU), model tends to overestimate price stability; reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to reflect auction-driven volatility.
